item.title: Baby with heart defect carried by surrogate must receive care, Texas court says
item.description: Surrogate McKenna West declined to get an abortion requested by the intended parents after the fetus she is carrying was diagnosed with a severe but treatable heart defect.

item.title: Trump Media sells $100,000 Truth Social data access, drawing scrutiny
item.description: Customers are paying up to $100,000 a month for faster access to Truth Social posts from President Trump and other top users of the social media platform.

item.title: Watch Live: Lindsay Clancy trial jury hears from mental health counselor
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's trial entered a 12th day Wednesday, with the jury hearing testimony from police and a mental health counselor.

item.title: CPI report shows inflation eased in July to a 3.4% annual pace
item.description: The CPI report was in line with economists' expectations, marking the second consecutive month with cooler price pressures.

item.title: Darline Graham and Ralph Norman head to runoff in South Carolina's Republican Senate primary
item.description: Darline Graham and Ralph Norman will face off in a runoff for the Republican Senate nomination in South Carolina. CBS News' Fin Gómez and Anthony Salvanto look at this and other key takeaways from Tuesday's contests.

item.title: Los Angeles Lakers to be sold to Bob Iger, Josh Kushner for $12.5 billion
item.description: The deal comes less than 1 year after Mark Walter purchased a majority stake from the Buss family for about $10 billion.

item.title: 11 charged for alleged sham marriages to help Chinese nationals get green cards
item.description: The Justice Department unveiled criminal charges alleging 11 people participated in a scheme that involved more than 1,000 "sham marriages" between Chinese nationals and U.S. citizens.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's mental health counselor says she did not see signs of her distress
item.description: Latiesha Dukes, one of Lindsay Clancy's mental health counselors before the deaths of her three children, testified Wednesday that she did not see signs of Clancy in crisis. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has the latest.

item.title: World Central Kitchen feeds families in Colombia after devastating earthquake
item.description: Families in Colombia are suffering after a catastrophic earthquake destroyed homes and killed more than 250 people. Response director Juan Camilo Jiménez explains how his organization is partnering with local groups to provide aid in the aftermath.

item.title: New space object called "black hole star" discovered by astronomers
item.description: The newly discovered object looks like a star the size of our solar system, but produces 100 billion times more energy than any star.

item.title: Top Trump officials heading to Iowa to help GOP campaigns, sources say
item.description: The upcoming Iowa State Fair is a pivotal window of opportunity for candidates on the campaign trail.

item.title: Inflation cools slightly; New York City Council probes prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket
item.description: U.S. inflation cooled slightly in new data from July. Also, the New York City Council launched a sweeping investigation into the marketing practices of prediction market companies such as Kalshi and Polymarket. Axios markets correspondent Matt Phillips shares his thoughts.

item.title: Total solar eclipse provides wonder, "connection with the universe" to viewers, astronomer says
item.description: The Perseid meteor shower will peak during 2026's only total solar eclipse. Director of astronomy at Adler Planetarium, Dr. Geza Gyuk, explains why the eclipse is so special.

item.title: Trump defends plane switch in Turkey as lawmakers demand more answers
item.description: President Trump defended his secret plane swap in Turkey after a credible Iran threat against Air Force One. Meanwhile, lawmakers are demanding more answers about it since administration officials and journalists remained on the threatened plane. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has more.

item.title: Instagram owner Meta accused of causing social media addiction in children in massive lawsuit
item.description: Tech giant Meta is being accused of designing social media platforms that violate privacy and enable social media addiction in children. Jury selection in the trial begins today. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more on the case.

item.title: How much time does AI save at work? New Census Bureau data breaks it down.
item.description: New Census data shows how much faster workers can complete tasks when they enlist artificial intelligence for help.

item.title: How much interest will a $15,000 high-yield savings account earn over the next year?
item.description: Moving $15,000 into a high-yield savings account makes sense now. Here's how much interest you can earn if you do.

item.title: Trump says U.S. has "total control" over Strait of Hormuz
item.description: President Trump said Wednesday that the U.S. has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz, writing on social media: "I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT."

item.title: NYC Council probes prediction markets over advertising practices
item.description: New York City lawmakers allege that four major prediction markets engage in deceptive marketing practices and target young adults.

item.title: Becky G on her friendship with Karol G: "Our goal is to be the best versions of ourselves"
item.description: Singer Becky G speaks with Gayle King about her tour with Karol G and the bond the two pop stars have formed. "We have a beautiful friendship," Becky G says, "one I'm really, really thankful for and one that I think throughout the years we've really earned with one another."

item.title: What happens after you miss three credit card payments?
item.description: Missing three consecutive credit card payments can put your finances at risk in ways that are difficult to undo.

item.title: Breaking down key primary race results in Minnesota and Wisconsin
item.description: Darline Graham and Ralph Norman are advancing to a runoff for Sen. Lindsey Graham's seat, CBS News projects. Meanwhile, moderate David Crowley defeated progressive candidate Francesca Hong in Wisconsin's gubernatorial primary. CBS News' Jonah Kaplan has more.

item.title: David Crowley beats progressive Francesca Hong in Wisconsin gubernatorial primary
item.description: David Crowley unexpectedly beat a progressive candidate in the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor, and will face Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany on the ballot in November.

item.title: $1 billion Powerball jackpot on the line in tonight's drawing. Here's what to know.
item.description: The jackpot is the eighth-largest Powerball prize ever.

item.title: Norah O'Donnell: What I learned from my doctor about menopause
item.description: Norah O'Donnell sat down with her own doctor, Rachel Rubin, to tackle the important topic of menopause: How your body changes, why women may be needlessly suffering, and what you can actually do about it.

item.title: Hospitals push for upfront payments as healthcare costs rise
item.description: Hospitals and other medical providers are increasingly asking for payment before providing care, collecting more of what patients might owe.

item.title: Dems pick nominees in key Wisc. districts as Sean Duffy's son-in-law wins GOP primary
item.description: National Democrats see two Wisconsin districts currently held by Republicans as up for grabs in November — the 1st and 3rd Districts. Here's how the primaries are shaping up.

item.title: Darline Graham, Ralph Norman advance to runoff in South Carolina GOP Senate primary
item.description: Sen. Darline Graham and Rep. Ralph Norman will face off in a runoff later this month for the South Carolina GOP Senate nomination, CBS News projects, as they vie to replace the late Sen. Lindsey Graham.

item.title: "Pink flags" of postpartum psychosis — and more takeaways from "Healthful"
item.description: Perinatal psychiatrist Dr. Uruj Kamal Haider and Kriti Lodha joined a special edition of "Healthful" to talk more about mental health conditions, including postpartum psychosis​.

item.title: Fall foliage maps show when peak color is expected across the U.S.
item.description: Maps show the best weeks in 2025 for leaf peeping across the U.S., with peak colors arriving as early as late September in some states.
